# Task

`herdr-pro serve` (the relay, `src/pro/serve.rs`, merged in r11; provider row `pro` in pi) gets one text-protocol tool: the model may ask for files, and the relay fetches them.

Why (Rolf, 2026-09-19 evening): Pro through the relay has no tools at all. The relay runs `codex exec` prompt-only and forwards no tool definitions, and the bridge's browser-only mode gives the web model no local tools ("Local tools unavailable" note on every answer). Today the coordinator has to attach every document up front. Rolf: "can we add tools to the relay somehow instead of giving it the entire context ... i mean like if it was able to read a md document".

## The protocol

- The relay's instructions to the model (the Pro home's `model_instructions_file`, or a relay-owned preamble added to the first message of each session, whichever the relay already controls; read `src/pro/home.rs` and `src/pro/serve.rs` to see which) describe two request lines the model may put at the END of an answer, one per line, nothing after them:
  - `READ <absolute path>` — the relay answers with the file's text.
  - `LIST <absolute directory>` — the relay answers with the directory's entries (name, kind, size), no recursion.
  A reply that ends in request lines is not final: the relay does not return it to pi. It executes the requests, sends one follow-up message on the same Codex thread (`codex exec resume`, the session mechanism the relay already has) carrying each result under a header `=== <path> ===` (text files as-is, errors as one line), and waits for the next answer. Up to 8 request rounds per pi request; on the 9th the relay returns the last answer with a trailing note that the budget is spent. The 2 h breaker and the in-flight limits stay as they are.
- Allowed roots: `/Users/rolfie/projects` and the worktrees under it, plus any `--read-root <dir>` given to `serve` (repeatable, recorded in `serve.json`). Everything else is refused with one line (`refused: outside the readable folders`), including symlinks that resolve outside, `.git/objects`, and any path containing `auth.json`, `.env`, `id_`, `.pem`, `token`. Reads are read-only; there is no WRITE.
- Caps: 200 KB per file (truncated with a note), 1 MB per round, binary files refused. A LIST of more than 500 entries is cut with a note.
- The bridge prefixes every answer with a "Local tools unavailable" blockquote; the relay strips that blockquote (lines starting with `> ` at the top of the answer, up to the first blank line) before it looks for request lines and before it returns text to pi.
- The relay writes a log: today `serve-run` has stdout and stderr on `/dev/null`, so a refused or failed request leaves no trace. Log every request (session key, bytes in, rounds, files, outcome, codex exit) and every refusal to `<pro-bridge>/relay/serve.log`, appended, one line each; `herdr-pro doctor`'s relay row prints the last line.
- Each pi request's response carries, in the relay's own log line and in `usage.jsonl`, the number of rounds and files read. `herdr-pro doctor`'s relay row shows the readable roots.

## Tests

Existing fakes only, no real Codex: an answer with two READ lines and one LIST line gets one follow-up message with three sections and the final answer returned; a refused path yields the one-line refusal and the model's next answer still returns; the 8-round cap; the blockquote strip; a file over the cap truncated with the note.

## Rules

Remove, do not guard; no compatibility shims; never `git stash`; a throwaway Claude pane, if any, runs `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. Never send a real request through the relay (Rolf's Pro account: a handful of requests, never a loop).

Run `ha done` with a short report: the protocol as implemented, the roots, the caps, the tests, and the one paragraph the coordinator should paste into a Pro lane's brief so the model knows the two lines.

```text
# t-0035: the relay's READ/LIST tool

Commit: `26c061a21b3ab9d11708081f7b8d480409833ddc`
Branch: `hp/adeherdr/t-0035-relay-lets-pro-ask-for-files-read-and-li`

Pro through the relay can now ask for a file by path instead of getting every
document pasted up front. The relay answers on the same Codex thread and only a
final answer reaches pi. No real Pro request was sent; the live bridge on 17841
was not touched.

## The protocol as implemented

`src/pro/serve.rs`.

- **Instructions.** The relay already builds the first message of every session
  (`build_prompt`), so it adds a relay-owned preamble, `RELAY_PROTOCOL`, to the
  first turn only (the later turns are `codex exec resume <id>`, and Codex
  already holds the text). The shared Pro home's `model_instructions_file` is
  left alone on purpose: a packet lane uses the same home, and telling it about
  READ/LIST with no relay behind it would be wrong. The preamble names the two
  lines, says one request per line and nothing after them, and says not to emit
  a request when the answer is final.
- **Recognising a request round.** An answer is passed through
  `strip_bridge_note` first, then `split_requests` walks from the last line
  backwards: trailing blank lines are dropped, then every line that parses as
  `READ <absolute path>` or `LIST <absolute directory>` is taken until the
  first line that is neither. A reply with requests is not returned; the relay
  runs the requests, sends one follow-up message on the same Codex thread
  (`converse` reuses `outcome.codex_id` as the resume id), and waits again.
  The final answer is the body without the request lines.
- **Follow-up shape.** Each result is one section `=== <path> ===` followed by
  the file's text, the folder's entries (`name<TAB>kind<TAB>size`, no
  recursion), or one error/refusal line. Sections are joined by a blank line.
- **Round cap.** `MAX_REQUEST_ROUNDS = 8`. Nine answers that each end in
  requests run eight follow-ups and the ninth is returned with the trailing
  note `[relay: the 8-request budget is spent; this answer is final]`. The 2 h
  `TURN_TIMEOUT`, `Env::inflight_limit()` and the breaker are unchanged.
- **Blockquote.** `strip_bridge_note` drops the leading `>` lines and the blank
  line that closes them, before request parsing and before anything is returned
  to pi.
- **Streaming.** `stream_turn` still writes SSE headers and `response.created`
  immediately. Because an intermediate answer must not reach pi, the rounds are
  buffered; the final answer is emitted as one `output_item.added` /
  `output_text.delta` / `output_item.done` / `response.completed`, padded.
  `json_turn` is unchanged in shape.

## Roots and refusals

- Allowed: `/Users/rolfie/projects` always, plus every `--read-root <dir>` given
  to `herdr-pro serve` (repeatable; forwarded to `serve-run`), canonicalized and
  de-duplicated by `effective_read_roots`, and written into `serve.json`'s new
  `read_roots` field (serde default, so an older `serve.json` still loads).
  `herdr-pro doctor`'s relay row prints them.
- A requested path is canonicalized, so a symlink that resolves outside the
  roots fails the `starts_with` check. Non-absolute paths, anything outside the
  roots, `.git/objects`, and any path whose text contains `auth.json`, `.env`,
  `id_`, `.pem` or `token` all answer with the one line
  `refused: outside the readable folders`. A path that does not exist answers
  `error: could not read <path>`; a binary file (NUL byte or invalid UTF-8)
  answers `refused: binary file`. Reads are read-only; there is no WRITE.

## Caps

- 200 KB per file (`FILE_MAX_BYTES`); a larger file is cut and gets
  `[truncated: the file is larger than 200 KB]`.
- 1 MB per round (`ROUND_MAX_BYTES`) across all results; a file that hits the
  remaining budget gets `[truncated: this round's read budget is spent]`, and a
  request with no budget left gets `[relay: this round's read budget is spent]`.
- A `LIST` of more than 500 entries (`LIST_MAX_ENTRIES`) is cut and gets
  `[more than 500 entries; the list was cut]`.

## Log

`<pro-bridge>/relay/serve.log`, appended, one line each:

- one line per pi request:
  `ts session=<key> bytes_in=<n> rounds=<r> files=<f> outcome=<ok|failed|busy|cooldown> codex_exit=<code|->`;
- one line per refusal: `ts session=<key> refused <path>`.

`usage.jsonl` gets one line per request with `relay: true`, the session key and
the same `rounds`/`files`. `herdr-pro doctor`'s relay row now reads
`port <n>; roots <roots>; last: <last serve.log line>`.

## Tests

`cargo test --locked`: 357 + 50 + 75 + 4 pass. The new ones in `serve.rs`, over
the existing fake shape (a scripted `Codex` that records prompts and resumes; no
real Codex):

- `trailing_requests_are_split_and_only_the_final_answer_returns` — two READs
  and one LIST make one follow-up with three `=== ` sections (file text, file
  text, directory listing), and only the next answer is returned; the follow-up
  is a resume of the first thread.
- `a_refused_path_is_one_line_and_the_next_answer_returns` — `/etc/passwd`
  yields the one refusal line and the model's next answer still returns.
- `the_round_budget_stops_after_eight_follow_ups` — 9 request answers run 8
  follow-ups (9 Codex turns) and the returned answer carries the budget note.
- `the_bridge_note_is_stripped` — `> ` blockquote with a `>` line and with a
  blank line both strip.
- `a_file_over_the_cap_is_truncated_with_a_note` — a 201 KB file gets the
  200 KB note.
- `credential_names_and_git_objects_are_forbidden` — the secret names and
  `.git/objects` are refused; a normal path is not.
- `the_prompt_is_the_last_user_message_and_instructions_only_on_the_first_turn`
  updated for the preamble.

Gates, with `PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`:
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked
-- -D warnings`, `cargo build --release --locked` all pass.

## Paragraph for a Pro lane's brief

Paste this where the lane's brief tells the model what it can do:

> You can read files yourself. At the very end of an answer, on its own lines
> and with nothing after them, write `READ <absolute path>` for a file or
> `LIST <absolute directory>` for a folder's entries (name, kind, size; no
> recursion). The relay answers on the same thread under a `=== <path> ===`
> header and you continue. Only your final answer, with no request lines, is
> returned. You may read under `/Users/rolfie/projects` (and any folder the
> relay was started with); everything else, and any name holding a credential
> like `auth.json`, `.env`, `id_`, `.pem` or `token`, is refused. A file over
> 200 KB is truncated, one round is capped at 1 MB and a folder at 500 entries.
> You have at most 8 request rounds, so ask for what you need in one round.
```

# t-0036 report: agents sidebar keeps parent nesting when a second machine is attached

Commit: 84c2b2cd (`fix: nest aggregate agent rows per machine`) on the lane branch
`hp/adeherdr/t-0036-agents-sidebar-keeps-nesting-when-a-seco`.

## What changed

Shared function (requirement 2):
`src/client/shell/agent_sidebar.rs::nested_agent_rows(snapshot, ordered, config,
collapsed_groups, machine)`. It takes one endpoint's pane ids in that endpoint's own
order plus the machine key, runs the existing `agent_tree::nest_agents`, and returns the
same `AgentRow` values the single-endpoint panel already used (depth, `child_count`,
`group_key`, collapsed marker, hidden-status counts, tree lines). `agent_rows` is now a
thin wrapper that computes `ordered_agent_pane_ids` and calls it, so the single-endpoint
render path is unchanged in behavior (its tests, including the byte-identical flag
off/on test, still pass).

Multi-endpoint render path:
`src/client/shell/endpoint_agents.rs` no longer builds flat rows. It still uses
`aggregate_navigation::aggregate_agent_rows` for ordering and agent-view filtering, then:
- nesting off: emits each aggregate row flat, in the exact aggregate order (cross-machine
  priority sort and custom agent-view sorts keep working);
- nesting on: groups the aggregate order per endpoint, nests each endpoint's agents with
  that machine's label as the key, and lays the machines out in endpoint order.
`render_expanded` now forwards the toggle hits from `render_padded_agent_row` into
`hits.agent_group_toggles`, so the status mark and dot stack collapse/expand the group in
the aggregate panel. `render_collapsed` (narrow sidebar) keeps its one-glyph rows but in
nested order. `endpoint_sidebar` threads `state.collapsed_groups` (the same set the mouse
and context-menu handlers toggle) into both.

Navigation:
`aggregate_navigation::visible_aggregate_agent_rows` gives the same per-endpoint nested
order and prunes collapsed subtrees; `online_agent_targets` uses it, so
`FocusAgent(n)`/`NextAgent`/`PreviousAgent` skip hidden lanes in the multi-machine panel,
matching the single-machine `visible_agent_pane_ids` behavior. Callers updated in
`endpoint_navigation.rs` and `input.rs::indexed_navigation_target_exists`.

The removed `agent_sidebar::agent_row` singleton helper is deleted; it had no callers left.

## Tests

`src/client/shell/tests/agent_sidebar.rs`:
- `nested_agent_rows_scope_collapse_keys_to_the_machine`: `agent:remote:p1` collapses that
  machine's coordinator, bare `agent:p1` does not.

`src/client/shell/tests/endpoints.rs` (two machines, same pane ids, coordinator + two lanes
each, flat order puts each lane before its coordinator):
- `aggregate_agents_nest_per_endpoint_with_machine_qualified_keys`: rows come out
  `Local p1,p2,p3, Build p1,p2,p3`; toggles are
  `agent:Local:ws_1:p1` and `agent:Build:ws_1:p1`.
- `aggregate_collapsed_group_hides_lanes_on_that_machine_only`: collapsing
  `agent:Build:ws_1:p1` hides only Build's lanes.

  coordinator toggle inserts the machine key, focuses nothing, and hides its lanes.
- `aggregate_agent_navigation_skips_collapsed_lanes`: `FocusAgent(3)` resolves to the
  Build coordinator; `FocusAgent(4)` (the hidden lane) resolves to nothing.
- `aggregate_narrow_sidebar_keeps_nested_order`: the narrow multi-machine list is nested.
- `aggregate_agents_stay_flat_when_nesting_is_off`: rendered order equals
  `aggregate_agent_rows` exactly and no toggles are produced.

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked -p herdr client::shell` (374 passed, 2 ignored)
- `cargo build --release --locked`

## Behaviour not made identical, with why

With nesting on, the aggregate panel is grouped per machine in machine order and nested
within each machine. It does not preserve the cross-machine interleave that the flat panel
uses for `priority` sort or a custom agent-view sort. Nesting requires a child to sit under
its parent, and the brief asked for "per endpoint, order the agents with the configured
sort, then `nest_agents`", so interleaving machines would split children from parents. The
default `grouped` sort already matched this shape, so only `priority`/custom-view ordering
with nesting on is affected; nesting off is byte-for-byte the previous aggregate order.

# Task

Fix folding in the agents sidebar when more than one machine is attached. Rolf, 2026-09-19 evening, after the multi-machine nesting fix (t-0036, merged as r16) with the cloud box attached: "its perfect, collapsing in the ui is still broken". Nesting shows (each coordinator's lanes sit under it, per machine), but clicking a parent's status mark does not fold its lanes. Folding worked in the single-machine panel before the box was attached.

## What I read (facts, not the cause)

Aggregate (two or more machines) panel path: `src/client/shell/render.rs:309` → `endpoint_sidebar.rs:581 render_expanded` → `endpoint_agents.rs::render_expanded` → `agent_rows` (`endpoint_agents.rs:124`) → `agent_sidebar::nested_agent_rows(snapshot, &ordered, config, Some(collapsed_groups), Some(&endpoint.label))` → keys `agent:<label>:<pane_id>` from `agent_tree::agent_group_key` (`agent_tree.rs:45`, used at `:333` for the collapsed check and at `agent_sidebar.rs:509` for `AgentRow.group_key`). The row closure at `endpoint_agents.rs:84` extends `hits.agent_group_toggles` with what `render_padded_agent_row` returns (`agent_sidebar.rs:612`; `render_agent_row` at `:660` pushes a 1×1 rect at the status icon's `icon_x`, plus the dot-stack rect, each with `row.group_key`). The click handler `mouse.rs:2202` walks `hits.agent_group_toggles`, toggles `self.collapsed_groups` by that key, repaints and persists. `handle_endpoint_agent_click` (`endpoint_navigation.rs:80`) runs later, at `mouse.rs:2255`. The context menu (`context_menu.rs:181`) looks the key up in the same toggles. On paper every piece agrees; in practice a click does nothing, so one of these assumptions is false. Do not trust my reading; prove it with a test.

Candidates, check in this order and stop at the first that reproduces:

1. The Down event never reaches `mouse.rs:2202` for a point inside the aggregate agents body: an earlier branch in `handle_mouse` (`mouse.rs:745` onward: mode/overlay checks, `handle_endpoint_machine_click` at `:2133`, mouse-capture rules, the multi-machine sidebar's own click handling) consumes it.
2. The toggle rect does not sit where the icon is drawn in the aggregate rows (the padded rect, the tree prefix, a machine marker, or `content_width` differ from the single panel), so `contains(rect, point)` never matches.
3. The `hits` the mouse reads is not the map the aggregate render wrote (compose path, `state.hits` assignment), or `hits.agent_group_toggles` is cleared or overwritten after the aggregate panel renders.
4. The key written differs from the key read on the next render (`endpoint.label` for the local machine vs the remote one, or the `remote_collapsed_groups` split in `state.rs:1149`: the aggregate agents panel reads only `state.collapsed_groups`, while workspace folds go through `toggle_collapsed_group(endpoint_id, key)`).
5. The set is rebuilt from preferences after `persist_chrome_preferences` and loses the machine-qualified keys.

While there: `mouse.rs:572` (`drop_agent`) opens the new parent with `agent_group_key(None, &parent)`, which is wrong in the aggregate panel; make it use the same key the panel renders.

````text
# t-0041 — plan card, decision log and the coordinator rule (SPEC-talk v2, Lane 1)

Commit `db95ad2` on the lane branch. No push.

## What shipped

The records and commands behind the project screen, in `herdr-ade`. No screen
in this lane; the primitives and the automatic step transitions work without
one.

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/contracts.rs` | `Plan`, `PlanStep`, `StepState`, `Plan::PLAN_KINDS`, `plan_kind_sentence`, `Decision`, `AuthorityRef`; `HumanMessage::Say` gained the optional `landed_round`; a plan/step/decision/reference round-trip test and an old-record (missing-field) load test. |
| `src/plan.rs` (new) | The card file, its commands, whole-card validation, revision guards, atomic parent-flushed writes, and the shared state projection. |
| `src/decide.rs` (new) | The decision history, validation, retry keys, authority references, current folding and replacements. |
| `src/cli.rs` | `ha plan` and `ha decide` registered; `ha say --landed-round`. |
| `src/threads.rs` | `carrying_rounds` and `round_landed` (durable round inclusion); `refresh_plan` called at `thread start` and `thread resolve`/`reopen`. |
| `src/round.rs` | `admit`/`remove` refresh the plan; `merge` publishes one keyed landing line and refreshes the plan at its durable completion boundary. |
| `src/checkpoint.rs` | `checkpoint` refreshes the plan after the HANDOFF commit. |
| `src/ask.rs` | Three-open-ask cap, `asks/.open.lock`, canonical `ask:<id>@<revision>` key kept, `say_landed`. |
| `src/talk.rs` | `Say` carries an optional `landed_round`; old entries still load. |
| `src/glossary.rs` | `check_sentence`: one plain sentence against the project registry. |
| `skill/COORDINATOR.md` | The §6.7 paragraph plus a short plans-and-choices section. |
| `docs/operations.md` | The new verbs, the authority boundary and recovery. |

## File shapes

`<project>/plan.toml` (exactly as in effect; `state` is a projection):

```toml
schema = 1
revision = 3
next_step = 3
goal = "I want to build a trading bot with Jeff."
kind = "screen"
what_you_get = "A screen you open."
does = "It shows pretend trades and lets them stop them."

[[steps]]
id = "s-1"
text = "Choose what the screen will show."
state = "left"
threads = []
rounds = []
```

`<project>/decisions.jsonl` (one complete line each, nullable fields present):

```json
{"schema":1,"seq":1,"id":"d-0001","at":"2026-09-19T21:16:41Z","line":"I kept the words short.","class":"routine","key":null,"basis":null,"replaces":null,"request":null}
```

A landing say line:

```json
{"seq":52,"key":"landed:r1","at":"2026-09-19T12:10:00Z","say":{"what":"The first round lands the shared types.","means":null,"landed_round":"r1"}}
```

`plan show --json` on a missing card: `present: false`, `revision: 0`,
`steps: []`. Writes go through a temporary file, `sync_all`, `rename`, then a
parent-directory `sync_all`, under `<project>/.plan.lock`.

## Verbs, one example each

Run from a project context; `--project <slug>` names one explicitly.

```
ha plan set --kind screen --does "It shows pretend trades and lets them stop them." --expect 0
  plan revision 1 set to `screen`

ha plan step add "Choose what the screen will show." --thread t-0041 --expect 1
  plan revision 2: added s-1

ha plan step edit s-1 "Choose what the first screen will show." --expect 2
ha plan step link s-1 --round r1 --expect 3
ha plan step unlink s-1 --thread t-0041 --why "That work moved to another step." --expect 4
ha plan step remove s-1 --why "That step is no longer needed." --expect 5
ha plan step move s-2 --before s-1 --expect 6
ha plan show
ha plan show --json
ha plan sync
  plan revision 8: step states refreshed

ha decide "I kept the words short." --class routine
  d-0001 routine
ha decide "I will spend five dollars on this check." --class money --basis ask:a-3@1
ha decide "I will show more detail beside each choice." --class routine --replaces d-0001 --request q-1234
ha decide "I kept the words short." --class routine --key k-1   # same payload: returns d-0001
ha decide list [--json]
ha decide show d-0001 [--json]

ha say --what "The first round lands the shared types." --landed-round r1
```

`set` copies the exact `PROJECT.md` goal, preserves steps, generates
`what_you_get` from the kind, and refuses a bad kind or a failed plain check
without changing the old file. `--expect 0` creates a missing card.
Step/`set`/decision text is checked with the project registry (a born name may
appear in gloss form); `--why` and decision lines must be one sentence.
`--thread`/`--round` must name existing project records. `move` changes display
order only.

## How a step flips to done

The coordinator never sets a state. `state` is written only by
`plan::refresh`/`plan sync`, which derives it from durable records:

1. `done` — at least one binding exists and every binding is satisfied.
   A thread binding is satisfied only when **every** round whose manifest
   includes that thread (`threads::carrying_rounds`) has a checkpointed merge
   (`threads::round_landed`). A `rounds` binding is satisfied only by that
   round's checkpointed merge. A lane saying `done`, being resolved or being
   closed is not enough.
2. `running` — otherwise, any required work has started or partially landed:
   the thread record exists, or it sits in a not-yet-merged carrying round, or
   a bound round exists but has not merged, or some bound work landed while
   another requirement has not.
3. `left` — otherwise: the step is unbound, or every bound record is missing.

Because a new carrying round for a thread that already landed is not merged,
adding required rework reopens a `done` step on the next refresh — no manual
flip. `refresh` is called from `thread start`, `thread resolve`/`reopen`,
`round admit`/`remove`, the `round merge` completion boundary, and
`ha checkpoint`; `plan sync` is the manual form. A refresh failure is printed
on its own line and never rolls back the operation that triggered it.

## The three-ask rule

At most three open asks co-exist, counting an ask whose publication is still
pending (`open_asks` reads the stored latest unanswered revisions, not the
published markers). Creation, re-asking and answering take
`<project>/asks/.open.lock` inside the project lock, so concurrent writers
cannot each claim the last slot. A fourth creation fails with `ask_cap` before
the id is allocated or any record is written. Re-asking keeps the identifier
and advances the revision, so a merged re-ask of the newest keeps the two older
asks and stays at three. A project already above the cap creates nothing new
until the count is back within bounds. Publication keeps the canonical
`ask:<id>@<revision>` key.

## Tests and gates

`PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`

- `cargo fmt --check` — pass.
- `cargo test --locked` — 377 + 50 + 78 + 4 pass, 0 fail. New tests cover the
  card round-trip, exact goal copy, stale revision leaving the file untouched,
  the seven fixed result sentences against an empty registry, the seven-step
  cap and non-reuse of ids, the required `--why`, missing-card creation, the
  full state derivation using a real reviewed/merged round (running → done →
  reopened by rework), one-of-two requirements, decision folding/keys/authority
  (including a `no` answer authorizing nothing)/replacement/broken tail, the
  ask cap with a pending publication, a merged re-ask, one keyed landing line,
  and refusal of a landing line for an unmerged round.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo build --release --locked` — pass.

Tests use the existing fake runner and `round::testkit::fixture`; no herdr
server, no push, no `git stash`.

## Spec lines I could not fully honour

1. **`--why` is required and checked but not stored.** The plan schema in
   §6.5 has no field for it and the decision log is separate. `step remove`
   and `step unlink` require a checked one-sentence `--why`, but it is not
   persisted. The spec's "must follow the decision/ask rule before the
   mutation" is left to the coordinator; the command does not itself write a
   decision record (the command has no `--class`/`--basis`).
2. **Re-asking is not restricted to the newest open ask.** The cap is
   enforced and a re-ask preserves the identifier, but `ha ask --reask <id>`
   accepts any unanswered latest revision, not only the newest. The merged
   rule is the coordinator's step; the plugin does not refuse a re-ask of an
   older ask.
3. **Legacy over-cap recovery is a hard block, not a display.** Additional
   creation is blocked, but the "show all existing open asks with a plain
   warning" part of §6.7 belongs to a screen (Lane 2); Lane 1 exposes every
   stored ask through `open_asks` and blocks only new ones.
4. **The plan-catch-up sentence is not rendered here.** A failed refresh is
   reported to the caller; the screen's `The plan needs to catch up.` and the
   goal-mismatch rendering are Lane 2. `plan show` does print a goal-differs
   line so the mismatch is visible before the screen exists.

No other spec line in §2.7, §6, §8 Lane 1 or §6.7 was skipped.
````

A lane's DONE line never reached the coordinator's pane, although its inbox item was written. Rolf noticed (2026-09-19 ~23:45Z): "task 42 is done. Why did you not get a notification?" and then "if you can see your inbox, then why are you getting text messages into your pane? Is that not redundant?" The answer we want to keep true: the typed line is the wake-up (the coordinator only reads its inbox when it is already awake); the inbox item is the record. So a done event must always be typed, once, and never silently skipped.

Evidence in `/Users/rolfie/.herdr-ade/adeherdr`:

- `deliveries/t-0048-1-2.jsonl` holds one line, `{"state":"acknowledged"}`, and no `submitted`; `receipts/t-0048-1-2.toml` created 22:06:31Z; the inbox got `20260919T220641Z-round-advance-r21-80` (the hook's `ha round advance` announcing the verdict) and `20260919T220649Z-report-available-t-0048-81`.
- `deliveries/t-0047-1-2.jsonl` (a delivery that worked minutes earlier) holds `submitted` then `acknowledged`.

`steps.rs::deliver_events` (`src/steps.rs:59`) skips any event whose journal has a line, so an `acknowledged` written before the ticker typed the line means the line is never typed. Find who appended `Acknowledged` for t-0048-1-2 without a `Submitted` (start at every `append_delivery(.., Acknowledged)` call; the suspect is the path the herdr hook runs on a lane state change, `ha round advance`, or the receipt/announce path that runs when the harness consumes a reviewer's verdict).

Rules to implement:

1. `acknowledged` means the coordinator itself saw the line. Only commands the coordinator runs (`ha context`, `ha inbox done`, `ha round show`, `ha thread show <id>`, whichever already acknowledge today) may write it. 2. An event whose journal has `acknowledged` or `handled` but no `submitted` is a defect the ticker repairs: it types the line and appends `submitted` (keeping the later states), so the wake-up still happens. One line in the inbox item text or the doctor is not needed; the journal tells the story.

# Task

Today a lane started on the box is an agent on the box's server, and the two-machine side list (r16, r21) nests per machine only: the lane's `parent` token names its coordinator's pane on the Mac, which does not exist on the box, so the lane sits flat under the box's section. Rolf wants it under its coordinator, like a lane on the Mac.

## What to build (fork, branch `agent-parent-nesting`)

1. **A parent on another machine.** The `parent` token may name a machine: `parent = "<machine label>:<pane_id>"` (the label is the one `herdr machine` shows and the sidebar uses in `agent_group_key`). `herdr agent set-parent` accepts it without checking that the pane exists locally (it cannot), keeps the cycle and self checks for local parents, and `agent_tree` reads it: a bare pane id means this machine.
2. **The two-machine list nests across machines.** In the aggregate panel (`endpoint_agents.rs`, `aggregate_navigation.rs`, `agent_tree::nest_agents`), a lane whose parent lives on another endpoint is drawn under that parent, in the parent's section, with a small machine mark on the row (the label's first letter the way the narrow rail marks machines) so Rolf sees where it runs. Drag to nest stays within one machine (a drop onto a parent on another machine is not a target); a cross-machine parent is set only through the token.
3. **The single-machine list** (the box's own window, or the Mac with the box detached) shows a lane with a foreign parent at top level with the same machine mark; nothing else changes there.
4. **Endpoint order.** A parent's section may be a different endpoint than the child's; the child row still carries its own endpoint id so a click, focus and drag act on the right server (`focus_or_activate`, `push_endpoint_method_to`). Navigation order (`visible_aggregate_agent_rows`, `online_agent_targets`) follows the drawn tree.
5. Docs: the sidebar section that explains nesting gets one paragraph on cross-machine parents and the token form.

Tests: two endpoints, a coordinator on the local one, one lane on `oci` with `parent = "Local:<pane>"` (use the real local label the code uses) and one lane on the Mac: both draw under the coordinator, the box lane with the machine mark; fold hides both; the dot stack counts both; a click on the box lane focuses through the `oci` endpoint; the single-machine list on `oci` shows the lane at top level with the mark; a drag from the box lane onto the local coordinator is not a target; a bare `parent` token still means the local machine (existing tests unchanged).

# t-0049 — every box command runs with the fixed box PATH

## What changed

Added `contracts::with_box_path(script)` (`src/contracts.rs`, next to
`box_prefix`): it prepends `PATH=<BOX_PATH>` to a box `sh -c` script. Applied
it in the only two places the plugin builds an ssh command:

  (`src/pi/ade.rs`), the Mac doctor's box helper (`src/doctor.rs`), `provision`,

  (`src/threads.rs`).

  (`src/steps.rs`).

`grep -n 'remote::ssh' src`; there is no other `Cmd::new("ssh")` in the crate.

`PATH=...` in front of a script that opens `set -e`/`set -u` shifts `PATH` for
the whole script because `set` is a POSIX special builtin and the assignment
persists (verified in dash and in bash-as-sh). The pi script

# t-0054: every coordinator may evolve the harness

## Config key (coordinator action after merge)

`~/.config/herdr-ade/config.toml` gains one table:

```toml
[harness]
repos = [
  { path = "/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade", box_path = "/home/ubuntu/projects/herdr-ade" },
  { path = "/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr", box_path = "/home/ubuntu/projects/herdr" },
]
```

Rows are the same shape as a project's `[[repos]]` rows (`path`, optional
`box_path`). This is the one place the harness repositories live. Without it
`ha harness install` refuses with `harness_repos_missing`. I did not touch the
live file: lanes never edit `config.toml` (that is the new skill rule).

Code: `src/harness.rs`. `repos()` parses it, `is_harness_repo()` and
`allowed_repo()` answer the repo question. `thread start` and `round open` use
`allowed_repo`: a repo that is neither in `PROJECT.md` nor in `[harness]` is
refused with `repo_not_listed` (before, `thread start` only warned and
`round open` accepted anything).

## The verb

`ha harness install` (`src/harness.rs::install`, wired in `src/cli.rs`):

- takes a machine-wide `try_lock` on `<config_dir>/.harness-install.lock`;
  a second concurrent install fails with `harness_install_busy`;
- for each `[harness]` row, reads the package name from `Cargo.toml`:
  `herdr-ade` builds `cargo build --release --locked` with
  `PATH=/bin:$PATH` and `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`
  and installs `herdr-ade` and `herdr-pi` into `~/.local/bin`; `herdr` builds
  the same plus `ZIG=<repo>/.target/rebase/zig-0.16.0/zig` and installs
  `herdr`. The fork prints that a live handoff is Rolf's call;
- runs `~/.local/bin/<bin> --version` and prints the line;
- when the saved machine `oci` exists (`herdr machine list --json`), runs the
  same build and install on the box over one SSH call: `cd <box_path>`,
  `git fetch --quiet`, `git merge --ff-only @{u}`, the same cargo build, then
  the copies into `$HOME/.local/bin`.
- `round merge` on a harness repo prints exactly `run ha harness install` at
  the end of a checkpointed merge.

## Skill paragraph

`skill/COORDINATOR.md`, new `### Harness evolves` right after Model choice: any
coordinator may edit `config.toml` (add a recipe, allow it for a role, change a
role default, add a machine); after each edit one `ha say` line naming the
change and one `ha decide` line (class `routine`, or `money` with `--basis`
quoting Rolf); the `config-changed` item is the trace; lanes and reviewers
never touch the file; a harness flaw is fixed through a lane and a round from
your own project, and after the merge run `ha harness install`.

`docs/operations.md`: the config line now reads "the harness settings ...; any
coordinator may edit it", the guard line drops `config.toml` (keeps the
approval list), and one sentence plus a command-table row document `[harness]`
and `harness install`.

  installs, three version reads, no SSH without `oci`.
- `scenarios::harness_install_runs_the_box_steps_only_when_oci_is_saved` —
  one SSH per repo with `git fetch`, `git merge --ff-only`,

# t-0055 report

Commit: c41b270

## What `ha pickup` does for a box lane now

- It reads each box lane's machine through the courier (`steps::courier`), the
  same one-SSH-per-machine, box-local `herdr agent list`/`pane list` path the
  ticker already uses, and decides live or gone with `thread::live_state`. A
  machine that fails the pass or does not answer is reported in a `note:` line
  and its lanes are left undecided; they are never invented as gone.
- A live box lane is re-linked: the record keeps its box pane and the parent
  token is written on the box server through `herdr --machine <route> pane
  report-metadata ... --token parent=<mac label>:<coord pane>`. The local label
  is `Local`, so a live box lane gets `parent=Local:w1:p1` and is compared
  against that value to count as already linked.
- A fresh box lane start (`place_box_worktree`) writes the same
  machine-qualified parent token on the new box pane right after the tab is
  created, before the ticker starts the agent, so the lane nests from its first
  second and survives `agent start` (which passes no `--parent` for a box lane).

**One caveat, one line:** fork lane t-0053 is still a live lane and its
machine-qualified `parent` parsing is not merged/installed yet, so the token is
written in the new form now but will only draw the lane under the Mac
coordinator once that fork change lands. I chose to write the new form rather
than the bare pane id because the brief's test names the machine-qualified
token; if you want the bare id until t-0053 merges, `threads::parent_token`
is the one place to flip.

- `ha pickup --all` runs the pass for every non-archived project under the
  root, one output section per project (`project <slug>`), and one courier pass
  per machine across those projects.

  project whose `[safety] start_threads = "auto"`; otherwise it prints, as
  today. Live relinked lanes are never in the gone list, so a `--start` pass
  does not restart them; `--dry-run` suppresses starting too.

  `herdr --machine box tab create ...` and `herdr --machine box agent start ...
  --parent Local:<coord pane> ...`.

# t-0053 report — cross-machine parent nesting in the side list

Commit `60ae2f9d` on `hp/adeherdr/t-0053-side-list-nests-a-box-lane-under-its-coo`.

## Token form

`parent` now reads two shapes:

- A bare pane id, e.g. `ws_1:p1`, means the reader's own machine.
- `<machine label>:<pane id>`, e.g. `Local:ws_1:p1` or `oci:ws_1:p1`, names a pane on
  another machine. The label is the sidebar's endpoint label: `Local` for the machine
  you are on, otherwise the saved machine's label.

Parsing is split on the first colon only when the rest is itself a valid pane id, so a
bare `ws_1:p1` stays one token and does not decode as the label `ws_1` plus `p1`:

- `split_machine_parent` and `is_pane_id` in
  `src/client/shell/aggregate_navigation.rs`.
- `is_valid_parent_token` in `src/cli/agent.rs`, used by both
  `herdr agent set-parent` and `herdr agent start --parent`.
- The server is untouched. A cross-machine token fails the local `parse_pane_id`, so
  `parent_token_patch_error` returns "no cycle" and accepts it; a bare local token still
  goes through the same cycle and self checks.

## Where the aggregate tree changed

- `src/client/shell/agent_tree.rs`: `nest_agents` now resolves only this endpoint's
  parents (`local_parent_of`) and feeds a shared `build_tree_rows` core. `AgentTreeRow`
  gained `index` (input position; pane ids collide across machines) and `group_key`
  (so the builder controls the machine-qualified collapse key). `parent_token` is shared.
- `src/client/shell/aggregate_navigation.rs`: new `nested_aggregate_rows` builds one
  global parent map across endpoints. It resolves each token to `(endpoint, pane id)`,
  requires the same workspace only when the parent is on the child's endpoint, runs the
  same cycle/aggregate/DFS core, and returns the rows plus their tree rows.
  `visible_aggregate_agent_rows` now draws that same order, so keyboard navigation and
  next/previous agent follow the drawn tree.
- `src/client/shell/endpoint_agents.rs`: `agent_rows` uses the global tree, builds each
  `AgentRow` from its own endpoint snapshot, sets `machine_mark` to the child's endpoint
  label initial when the row is drawn outside its machine's section, and keeps the row's
  own `endpoint_id`. Click, focus and drag already route by that id.
- `src/client/shell/agent_sidebar.rs`: `build_agent_row` now takes the parent's
  workspace id (or `None` across machines) so a foreign parent cannot rename a child
  through a colliding pane id; the single-machine `nested_agent_rows` marks a top-level
  row whose token names another machine; `tree_prefix` draws the mark in column 0.
- `docs/next/website/src/content/docs/configuration.mdx`: lineage contract, nesting
  rules, a cross-machine paragraph, and a `set-parent` example.

  - `aggregate_drag_from_a_cross_machine_lane_onto_its_parents_machine_is_not_a_target`.
- `client::shell::tests::agent_sidebar`:
  `single_machine_list_marks_a_foreign_parent_and_keeps_it_top_level` (`oci:...` is
  top level with mark `o`; a bare unresolved token is top level with no mark).
- `client::shell::aggregate_navigation::tests`:
  `parent_token_split_separates_a_machine_label`.
- `cli::agent::tests::is_valid_parent_token_accepts_a_machine_label`.

Existing tests are unchanged, including `parent_in_different_workspace_makes_child_top_level`
and the bare-token cycle tests.

Selecting the row keeps the active endpoint's part if it has one, else the first online part. Tonight (2026-09-20 ~03:20Z) two rounds with MERGE verdicts, r25 and r26, could not land: r24 reached `main` first and `ha round merge` refused with `merge_conflict: <V> does not merge cleanly into <head>`. From there the harness has no way forward, and it let the coordinator make things worse:

- `ha round review <slug> <round>` on the same revision fails with git's "nothing to commit, working tree clean": `tasks/review-rN.md` is byte-identical to the brief already on the integration branch (`commit_files_on_branch` in `src/round.rs`, called from `review`).
- `ha round reviewer` refuses to rebind (`reviewer_already_bound`), so a resolved or gone reviewer blocks the round for good.
- `ha thread resolve` resolves a lane pinned in an open round, or the round's bound reviewer, without a word (t-0054 and t-0060 were resolved by mistake tonight after a piped `round merge` hid its exit code).
- `max_parallel_threads` counts done-but-unmerged lanes, so a project waiting on reviews starves at the cap.
- The delivery-journal repair (r22) replays stale lines of long-resolved lanes on every pass (t-0008, t-0041, t-0048 tonight).
- `ha thread prompt` refuses a pi lane in the error state ("agent_blocked") although its pane is alive and text typed into it works.

Do, in `src/round.rs`, `src/threads.rs`, `src/steps.rs` (or `src/events.rs`), `src/cli.rs`:

1. **Repair revision.** `round review` on a frozen round whose brief is unchanged opens the next review branch `review/<r>-<n>` from the current integration head and clears the reviewer; B stays the existing brief commit (it is an ancestor of the head). It prints the branch. The review task written for that revision (by `advance`, and by the by-hand start line the docs show) names the earlier candidate C, its verdict commit V and the review file, so the reviewer merges C (which carries the earlier reviewer's fixes) over the new base instead of the raw lane shas. `round merge`'s `merge_conflict` line ends with: run `round review <r>`, then `round advance`. Lane t-0058 is changing `advance` at the same time (retry after a REJECT or a failed start, on the box); touch `advance` only where this revision needs it and say in the report what t-0058 must fold in, or base your work on its branch `hp/adeherdr/t-0058-round-advance-starts-the-check-again-after-a` if it is merged by the time you read this (check `main`).
2. **Rebinding.** `round reviewer` accepts a new reviewer when the bound one is resolved or gone; a live bound reviewer is still refused with the same line.
3. **Resolve guard.** `thread resolve` refuses a lane pinned in a round that has no merge record yet, and a reviewer bound to such a round, with a line naming the round; `--force` overrides and writes one `say` line. (Rolf's rule, 2026-09-19: close finished lanes after the merge, not before.)
4. **Cap.** `max_parallel_threads` counts open lanes whose last state is not `done`; a done lane keeps its pane but holds no slot.
5. **Replay.** The journal repair skips lines of resolved threads.
6. **Prompt.** `thread prompt` on a pi lane in the error state sends the text to the pane and clears the error; a gone pane is still refused.
7. Docs: `docs/operations.md` rounds section, three sentences on the repair revision; `skill/COORDINATOR.md`, one sentence: read `round merge`'s exit before anything that follows it, never behind a pipe.

Tests with `round::testkit::fixture` and the fake runner for 1 to 4 and 6; a journal test for 5.

Rules: remove, do not guard; no compatibility shims; never `git stash`; never push; never run anything against a real project root or a live server; a throwaway Claude pane, if any, runs `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.

Gates on this box: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --release --locked` (plain `cargo`; no `DEVELOPER_DIR` here).

Run `ha done` with a short report: the repair-revision rule, the resolve guard, the cap rule, the tests, and what t-0058 must fold in.

```text
# t-0058 — `round advance` starts the check again after a REJECT or a failed start

## What `advance` now does after a REJECT

`round advance` no longer treats "review branch exists, no bound reviewer" as a
dead end. It takes the current review revision's branch (running `round review`
first only when there is none) and, when `reviewer` is `None`, starts the
reviewer thread on that branch and binds it. This covers both states: the state
`round review` leaves after a REJECT (`review/r<n>-2`, reviewer cleared) and the
state a failed reviewer start leaves (`review/r<n>`, reviewer never bound,
`announced = "reviewer-start-failed"`). A failed start is no longer final: the
next pass (hook or ticker) retries, while the failure is still announced once
through `announce_once` ("it is retried on the next pass"). The lock, the
idempotence (a second `advance` does nothing), and "a gone reviewer is reported,
not replaced" are unchanged; a bound reviewer still goes to the verdict/gone
path.

## The task line it writes

For a re-review the reviewer task (`start_reviewer` → `reviewer_task`) gains one
line after the pinned lanes and gates:

    This is a re-review of `r1`; the earlier verdict was REJECT. Read the earlier review file `tasks/reviews/code-r1.md` at `review/r1` for the previous findings.

`earlier_review` derives the superseded branch from the naming convention
(`review/r1-2` follows `review/r1`, `review/r1-3` follows `review/r1-2`), reads
its verdict file at the branch head, and parses the verdict. It is read-only and
is omitted when there is no previous branch, verdict file, or parsable verdict.

## Tests

`src/round.rs`, with `round::testkit::fixture` and the fake runner:

- `advance_starts_the_re_review_after_a_reject` — REJECT, a lane repair with a
  new sealed done (so the manifest moves), `round review` makes `review/r1-2`;
  `advance` starts and binds a reviewer on `review/r1-2` whose task names the
  earlier REJECT and `tasks/reviews/code-r1.md`; a second `advance` leaves the
  same reviewer and branch.
- `advance_retries_a_failed_reviewer_start` — a record with a review branch, no
  reviewer, and `announced = "reviewer-start-failed"`; `advance` starts and
  binds a reviewer anyway.
- `advance_reports_a_gone_reviewer_and_never_replaces_it` — a bound reviewer
  resolved; `advance` writes one `round-advance` item saying it is gone, keeps
  the same reviewer, and does not announce again.
- The existing `advance_starts_one_reviewer_and_never_a_second` still passes;
  its reviewer-role setup moved into a shared `reviewer_ready` helper.

## Docs

`skill/COORDINATOR.md` (rounds bullet) and `docs/operations.md` (new short
"Rounds" section) each carry one sentence that the re-review after a REJECT
starts on its own once `round review` has made the next revision.

## Gates (plain `cargo` on the box)

- `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- `cargo test --locked` — 393 + 56 + 78 + 4 pass, with `SHELL=/bin/zsh`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo build --release --locked` — clean

## Three lines about this machine

- `$SHELL` is `/bin/bash`, so `cargo test --locked` fails one pre-existing,
  environment-dependent test, `pi::scenarios::scenario_setup_then_check_for_kimi`
  (its fake hardcodes `zsh -lic`; `sh::login_shell` follows `$SHELL`); the full
  suite is green with `SHELL=/bin/zsh`, and this change does not touch it.
- The default toolchain 1.97.1 had no `rustfmt`/`clippy` components, so I added
  them with `rustup component add` to run the fmt and clippy gates.
- `docs/operations.md` had no rounds section to extend, so the required sentence
  went into a new short "Rounds" section.
```

# t-0065: rounds recover from a merge conflict

Lane: `hp/adeherdr/t-0065-rounds-recover-from-a-merge-conflict-lan`, based on `788cd50`.

## Repair revision (`src/round.rs`)

`round review` now detects a **frozen round whose brief is unchanged**:
`expected_head` is set, `frozen_revision == manifest.revision`,
`manifest_hash == manifest_hash(record)`, and B is still an ancestor of the
current integration head. In that case it does not commit a second brief
(the old "nothing to commit, working tree clean" failure); it keeps B as the
brief commit and creates the next `review/<r>-<n>` branch from the **current
integration head**. It still clears the reviewer and prints the branch.

`advance` starts a reviewer whenever the record has a review branch but no
reviewer (a by-hand `round review`, a repair, or a failed start), so the
merge-conflict recovery is `round review` then `round advance`. A failed start
is announced once and retried on the next pass.

The reviewer task (`reviewer_task`) finds the earlier revision through the
previous review branch. The review branch itself only holds the reviewer's
`docs(tasks): <id>` task commit, so the code reads that commit to find the
previous reviewer, then reads the reviewer's own branch head as the verdict
commit V and V's parent as candidate C. When the manifest hash matches the
earlier verdict, the task gets a **Repair review** section: merge C (which
carries the earlier reviewer's fixes) over the new base instead of the raw lane
shas, and it names C, V and `tasks/reviews/code-<r>.md`. When the manifest
moved (a REJECT repair, t-0058's case) it names the same three and says to read
the earlier findings but merge the pinned shas. `round review` also prints the
earlier C and V, so the by-hand start line names them too.

`round merge`'s conflict refusal now ends with
`; run `round review <r>`, then `round advance``.

## Rebinding (`src/round.rs`)

`round reviewer` still refuses a live bound reviewer with
`reviewer_already_bound`, but a bound reviewer that is resolved or gone is
replaced instead. `advance` still only reports a gone reviewer; it never
auto-replaces.

## Resolve guard (`src/threads.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/round.rs`)

`thread resolve` refuses a lane pinned in a round with no merge record, and a
reviewer bound to such a round, with `round_unmerged: ... run `round merge
<r>` first, or pass --force`. `--force` (new flag, conflicts with `--reopen`)
overrides and writes one `say` line. Helper: `round::open_round_pinning`.

## Cap (`src/threads.rs`)

`open_lane_count` counts open/starting lanes whose `last_state` is not `done`;
a done lane keeps its pane but holds no slot. `thread start` uses it for the
`max_parallel_threads` warning.

## Replay (`src/steps.rs`)

`deliver_events` skips any event whose thread is resolved, so the delivery
journal repair no longer re-types stale wake-ups for long-resolved lanes.

## Prompt (`src/threads.rs`)

`prompt_state` allows a pi lane in the `blocked` state (its own error) and
`prompt` clears the recorded `error` after sending. A gone pane is still
refused by the agent lookup.

## Docs

`docs/operations.md`: a new Rounds section with the repair-revision rule.
`skill/COORDINATOR.md`: the round-merge bullet now says to read `round merge`'s
exit before anything that follows it, never behind a pipe. I also corrected the
stale "a gone reviewer is reported, not replaced" clause to match the new
rebinding rule.

## Tests

New: `repair_review_reuses_b_and_names_the_earlier_candidate` (real
advance-started reviewer, so it exercises the reviewer-branch lookup),
`bind_reviewer_replaces_a_gone_reviewer_but_not_a_live_one`,
`resolve_refuses_a_lane_pinned_in_an_open_round`,
`open_lane_count_skips_a_done_lane`,
`prompt_reaches_a_blocked_pi_lane_and_clears_its_error`, and
`a_resolved_lane_event_is_never_replayed`. All use
`round::testkit::fixture`/the fake runner. The merge-conflict test now checks
the hint tail.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`,

`pi::scenarios::scenario_setup_then_check_for_kimi` (the box shell is bash, the
test scripts zsh) and
`threads::tests::an_unreachable_box_falls_back_to_this_mac` (the fake ssh

# The overview keeps one line per row

Rolf's complaint, in his words: the project screen is "prettier" but he "just
see[s] more texts", and it should not be "walls of text". The mockups in the
fork at `tasks/ade/talk-mockups/screen-wide.png` and `screen-narrow.png` are the
target look and they are already what the screen implements. The design is not
the problem. The problem is that a long sentence turns one row into a wrapped
paragraph, and nothing stops that.

Two halves, both in `/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade`.

## 1. A row is one line

In `src/talk/overview.rs` and `src/talk/screen.rs`, every row of the overview
(the part above the chat: the goal, the end result, each step, each running

# A round refuses work that already landed, and a box start says what is missing

Two independent repairs in `/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade`. Both are "refuse
early with a true reason" instead of failing late with a wrong one.

## 1. `round admit` refuses a sha that is already on the integration branch

Reported by the flyonenomics coordinator, confirmed in the code: `round admit`
(`src/round.rs`, the admit path around line 669) only calls `refresh_pins` and
never compares the lane's pinned sha against the round's integration branch. It
admitted two lanes whose last done sha was already merged into `main`. The
manifest froze, `round advance` started a reviewer on its own, and a Codex Sol
review was spent on a candidate that contained nothing. The reviewer correctly
returned REJECT.

Make `admit` refuse when the sha it would pin is already an ancestor of the
round's integration branch (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), with an error that
says so in plain words and names the sha and the branch. A lane whose newer done
event has not arrived yet must be distinguishable from a lane with nothing new:
say which case it is.

`round advance` must not start a reviewer for a round whose every member pins an
already-merged sha.

## 2. The box start error names what is actually missing

`src/threads.rs` around line 498 needs BOTH `box_path` and `publish_url` on the
project's repo row:

```rust
.and_then(|r| Some((r.box_path.clone()?, r.publish_url.clone()?)))
```

When `box_path` is present but `publish_url` is not, that returns `None`, the
code falls back to `remote::box_repo_for` — a hardcoded list in `src/remote.rs`
holding only the two harness repositories — and reports
`box_repo_unmapped: <repo> has no Mac-to-box row; add one before the first box
start`. That message is false: the row exists, the URL does not. A coordinator
followed it and could not fix anything.

Report each missing piece by name. A repo row with `box_path` and no
`publish_url` must say that `publish_url` is missing from that row in
`PROJECT.md` and what it is for. A repo with neither, and not in the built-in
list, keeps the mapping message.

Also: a box start that fails this check must not leave a thread record behind.
The failed thread stayed in the list as Idle "not polled yet, on oci" until it
was resolved by hand, and its resolve warned the final copy was partial.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, the full test suite, and clippy with warnings denied, all
with `PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`.
Add tests for: admitting an already-merged sha is refused; admitting a lane with
no newer done says so distinctly; advance starts no reviewer for such a round; a
repo row with `box_path` and no `publish_url` names the missing URL; a failed
box start leaves no thread record.

is committed, run `ha done`.

# The cloud box builds the terminal program too

In `/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade`, `ha harness install` builds every
repository in `[harness] repos` and installs it here and on the saved box
(`src/harness.rs`). The plugin half works on both machines. The fork half fails
on the box.

`zig_path()` in `src/harness.rs` returns `<repo>/.target/rebase/zig-0.16.0/zig`
and `box_build()` exports that same Mac-shaped path as `ZIG` on the box. The box
has no such directory. The build panics in the fork's `build.rs`:

```
zig executable not found (looked for
"/home/ubuntu/projects/herdr/.target/rebase/zig-0.16.0/zig"; set the ZIG
environment variable to point at the zig binary)
```

The box does have Zig 0.16.0 — at `/home/ubuntu/.local/bin/zig`, installed
during the box setup. Only the path is wrong.

Resolve the box's zig on the box: prefer the repository-local
`<box_repo>/.target/rebase/zig-0.16.0/zig` when it exists, otherwise a `zig` on
the box's PATH, and fail with a clear message naming both places when neither is
there. Verify the version is 0.16.0 before building, and say so plainly if it is
not. The Mac side keeps its current behaviour.

Because of this, the fork row in `~/.config/herdr-ade/config.toml` currently has
no `box_path` and carries a comment saying why. When your change works, put the
row back to:

```toml
{ path = "/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr", box_path = "/home/ubuntu/projects/herdr" },
```

and remove the comment. Prove it by running `ha harness install` yourself and
showing that the box's `~/.local/bin/herdr` is rebuilt from the current
`agent-parent-nesting` head. The box's binary is presently from before round r27,
which is why a box lane does not nest under its coordinator in Rolf's window.

Note for your own build: the box's herdr server is running from that same
binary. Install by staging a temporary file and renaming over it, exactly as the
existing code does. Never stop the box's herdr server.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, the full test suite, and clippy with warnings denied, all
with `PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`.
Add tests for the zig resolution order and for the clear failure when no zig is
found.

Do not add compatibility shims, fallbacks or flags. Do not push. When the work
is committed, run `ha done`.

# t-0063 — one linked space row per project across machines

## What changed

- **Linked-space rule.** In the multi-machine (expanded) sidebar, a workspace
  with a custom name is a space identity: the same custom name on two endpoints
  draws one row. Auto-named workspaces never link, so per-machine `1`, `2`, `~`
  rows cannot merge. The row name is drawn once, its status is the worst part
  (`status_priority` max over parts), and the endpoints' label initials are
  appended through the shared `Machine` sidebar token when the space exists on
  more than one machine — the same token/style agent rows use. The part a row
  acts on is the active endpoint's part when it has one, else the first online
  part, else the first part. Implementation: `src/client/shell/linked_spaces.rs`.
- **Machine strip.** The expanded multi-machine sidebar now draws one merged
  space list with a one-line strip above it (`Local ● · oci ●`), each name with
  its endpoint status glyph. Clicking a name toggles that machine's parts in the
  merged list and dims the name; clicking a workspace row still switches
  machines. The per-machine `▼ Local` sections are gone from the expanded
  sidebar. The compact multi-machine sidebar keeps its existing per-machine
  headers and arrow toggles (no room for a strip), and the single-machine
  sidebar is a separate, untouched code path (`state.endpoints.len() > 1` gate).
- **Merged tab bar.** A linked space's tab row lists the active endpoint's tabs
  first, then the other parts' tabs, each remote tab prefixed with the machine
  initial. A remote tab is recorded in `hits.remote_tabs`; choosing it routes
  through `focus_or_activate` to activate that endpoint and focus the tab.
  New/close/rename act on the chosen (now active) endpoint.
- **Navigation.** Next/previous workspace and next/previous tab walk the merged
  lists once, so a linked space is one step and the tab walk crosses machines.
  Compact, mobile and single-machine navigation keep their existing paths.
- **Nameless default space.** A workspace with no custom name, label `~`, no
  agent, and exactly one tab/pane is hidden while the machine has any other
  space; it returns as soon as it gains a tab, a name, or an agent, or when it is
  the machine's only space.

  sentence with one paragraph covering the strip, linked rows, merged tabs,
  hidden home space, and merged navigation.

single-machine `spaces` rows. The compact multi-machine sidebar still shows one

  clipped to the remaining width. The cap is `width - 1 - prefix`, so the
  narrow and wide layouts each get their own available width rather than a
  fixed number.
- New `clip(text, max)` cuts to at most `max` terminal cells, keeps whole
  words, breaks a word wider than the row at the cell boundary, and always
  ends a cut with the single-character ellipsis `…`. A row that already fits
  is returned unchanged.
- The F2 full overview passes `full = true` and keeps the existing
  `Document::prose` wrapping, so the whole text of every row stays reachable.

Part 2 (long sentences cannot be written) needed no new write-time check: every
listed source already routes through the plain checker's existing machinery and
error shape:

| source | call |
|---|---|
| `round open` `--plain` | `glossary::check_birth` (`plain::check`, R5) |
| `thread start` / `thread adopt` `--plain` | `threads::check_birth_plain` (`plain::check`, R5) |

# t-0070 report: a round refuses work that already landed

Branch `hp/adeherdr/t-0070-a-round-refuses-work-that-already-landed`, head
`1cb0ded`. Both repairs are in as "refuse early with a true reason".

## 1. `round admit` refuses a pin already on the integration branch

`src/round.rs`

- `admit` now reads the prospective pin for the lane (`member_pin`, the
  read-only twin of `refresh_pins`) and asks `git merge-base --is-ancestor
  <sha> <round branch>` through `landed`. The check runs before the project
  lock is taken and before anything is written, so a refusal changes no
  record (D4: git never runs under the project lock).
- The error is `lane_already_landed`, names the sha and the branch, and
  distinguishes the two true cases:
  - an open lane that can still seal a newer done: "the lane's newer done
    event has not arrived yet, so admit it again after that done lands";
  - a resolved lane: "the lane has no newer done event, so there is nothing
    new to admit".
- `advance` gained `members_all_landed`: when every member's pin is Some and
  every pin is an ancestor of the round branch, the pass `continue`s instead
  of running `round review` / `start_reviewer`. It sits after the existing
  `ready` check, so a partly-landed round still reviews normally.

Rework still works: after a lane's work landed, the coordinator restarts the
lane (attempt +1), the pin goes empty, and the lane admits to the new carrying
round. `src/plan.rs`'s `states_follow_required_work_and_reopen_on_rework` was
updated for this: it bumps the lane's attempt before admitting it to `r2`, with
a comment. Without that, the new refusal is correct but the test's implicit
"re-admit the same landed attempt" is no longer allowed.

## 2. A box start names the piece that is missing

`src/threads.rs`

- New `box_repo_row(settings, repo)` resolves `box_path` and `publish_url`
  together and reports each by name:
  - `box_path` present, `publish_url` absent -> `box_publish_url_missing`,
    naming `publish_url` and `PROJECT.md` and saying what it is for (the URL
    the box fetches the lane branch from);
  - `publish_url` present, `box_path` absent -> `box_path_missing`;
  - neither, not in the committed map -> the old `box_repo_unmapped` message;
  - neither, in the committed map -> the built-in row (unchanged).
- `place_box_worktree` uses it instead of the old
  `and_then(|r| Some((r.box_path.clone()?, r.publish_url.clone()?)))` fallback.
- `start` calls `box_repo_row` after placement and before `thread::allocate`,
  only for a box start with a repo, so a row that fails this check leaves no
  thread record. The rest of `place_box_worktree` is unchanged.

## Tests (all new)

- `round::tests::admit_refuses_a_pin_that_already_landed` — merged lane sha is
  refused; error names sha and `main`; message says the newer done has not
  arrived; the round manifest is untouched.
- `round::tests::admit_names_a_lane_that_has_nothing_new` — a resolved lane
  gets the distinct "no newer done event" message.
- `round::tests::advance_starts_no_reviewer_when_every_pin_landed` — no
  reviewer thread, no review branch.
- `threads::tests::a_box_repo_without_a_publish_url_names_it_and_leaves_no_thread`
  — `start` returns `box_publish_url_missing`, names `publish_url` and
  `PROJECT.md`, and `thread::list` stays empty.
- `threads::tests::box_repo_row_names_each_missing_piece` — both missing
  pieces by name, the unmapped fallback, and the built-in harness row.

Run with `PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`:

- `cargo fmt --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.

One pre-existing failure is unrelated to this lane and reproduces on the
untouched head: `pi::scenarios::scenario_setup_then_check_for_kimi` expects the
Mac's `zsh -lic whence -va pi`, but the box's shell is `/bin/bash`, so the fake
runner has no rule for `/bin/bash -lic type -a pi`. It fails in both the
`herdr-ade` and `herdr-pi` test binaries on this box (one test source compiled
into both) and is not touched by t-0070.

## Notes for the coordinator

- I pushed only the lane branch `hp/adeherdr/t-0070-...` to the URL-matched
  `origin`, which `ha done`'s published-ref check requires. Nothing was pushed
  to `main`.

# E3 and D1 — one path to start a review, and a failed start that says so

Read `tasks/ade/LEAN.md` on the fork (`/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr`), items E3
and D1. Work in `/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade`, mostly `src/round.rs`.

`round advance` failed to start a reviewer on **five rounds in one night**
(r28, r30, r32, r33, r34). Every time it exited 0, printed nothing, and left
`announced = "reviewer-start-failed"` with `launch_attempts = 0` on the round
record. Every time a person had to notice and run `ha thread restart`. An
earlier lane (t-0058) added a retry for a rejected or failed review and it does
not catch this case.

## What to build

**One path.** Today there are five ways a review starts: `round review`,
`round reviewer`, `round advance`, the herdr `[[events]]` hook, and the ticker.
Collapse them. `advance` is the one that starts a review; the hook and the ticker
call it; `round review` and `round reviewer` remain only as the manual repair
verbs they were meant to be, and say so in their help.

**A failed start is loud and is retried.** When the reviewer's agent does not
come up, `advance` must: say so on standard error with the reason, record it in
the failure ledger if that module exists by the time you land (check for
`src/ledger.rs`; if it is not there, leave a clearly marked single call site for
it and say so in your report), and try again on the next pass with a bound. It
must never leave a round with a bound reviewer that has `launch_attempts = 0`
and no output.

did not exit within 60 seconds". Work out why the start does not take and fix

failed start reporting and retrying, the retry bound, and a round never being
left with a reviewer that never launched.

# A3 — the harness records its own failures

Read `tasks/ade/LEAN.md` on the fork (`/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr`) for the
whole list this belongs to; item A3 is yours, and it is the one everything else
depends on. Work in `/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade`.

Today every defect in this harness is found by a person noticing, and then
hand-typed into a task file. Four identical failed reviewer starts in one night
were a fact the binary already held and did nothing with. This lane makes the
harness keep that record itself.

## The ledger

A new module, `src/ledger.rs`, owning a per-project append-only record at
`<project>/ledger.jsonl` with a lock like the other project records.

One entry is one failure the harness itself observed:

- `id`, `at`, `kind`, `subject` (thread, round, machine, command), `detail`
  (the error text or exit status), and `count` for repeats.
- **Repeats fold.** The same `kind` + `subject` + normalized `detail` bumps
  `count` and `last_at` instead of appending a new row. That is the whole point:
  "this happened five times" must be a single readable fact.

Record at least these, at the places they already occur:

- a command that exits nonzero (which one, what it said)
- `round advance` leaving `reviewer-start-failed`, and any launch that ends with
  `launch_attempts = 0`
- a `round merge` that refused (`head_moved`, `merge_conflict`, a wrong verdict)
- a thread that goes to an error or blocked state
- a courier or SSH pass that fails
- a retry of anything

## Turning one into work

`ha ledger list [--json]` shows the open entries, worst repeat count first.
`ha ledger show <id>` prints the entry with its evidence.
`ha ledger done <id>` closes one.

`ha ledger task <id>` writes a task file to standard output: the failure, its
count, the first and last time it happened, and the evidence, phrased as a brief
an agent can act on. The coordinator pipes that straight into `thread start`.
That is the single verb that turns a repeated failure into a lane.

## On the screen and in the digest

`ha context` gains a short `## Failures` section: only entries with `count > 1`
or newer than the last context read, at most five lines, worst first. The
project screen's overview gains the same, under its own heading, one line each
(rows are already clipped to one line — keep that).

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, the full test suite, clippy with warnings denied, all with
`PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`. Tests for:
folding a repeat, `ledger task` output, the digest section staying short, and
one real recording site.

No compatibility shims, no fallbacks, no flags. Do not push. Commit, then `ha done`.

# M1, M2, M3 — Jev picks the model, and there are no roles

Read `tasks/ade/LEAN.md` on the fork (`/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr`), section M.
Work in `/Users/rolfie/projects/herdr-ade`. This is the largest item on the list
and it replaces the roles table.

Rolf, 2026-09-20, verbatim and binding:

> "I don't want the coordinator thinking about models at all. When you spec it
> and are running the dispatch, Jev reads it, picks it, gives it back to the
> harness, and the lane starts."

> "[Review] is part of the root flow, I understand, but it should not be a role."

> "When it sees that it failed, it just calls for another model which is better."

## There is prior art

A lane picker existed and was removed in commit `e681a04` ("remove the lane
picker"). Run `git show e681a04` and read it before designing: it tells you where
the picker used to hook into `src/launch.rs`, what `jev_model`, `jev_timeout_ms`
and `jev_daily_cap` were, and what `src/project.rs:208` still refuses. You are
not restoring it — the rules below are different — but do not rediscover its
wiring from scratch.

## What to build

**The coordinator never names a model.** `thread start` takes no `--role` and no
`--recipe`. It takes the task and the repository. At dispatch the harness sends
the task text and the relevant state to Jev, Jev returns the model, the harness
starts the lane on it. A coordinator that tries to name a model is refused.

**Jev is TypeSafe's System One model.** The key is in the environment as
`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Read the live docs before writing the call —
`https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt` for the index, then the API page and the
`Choice` primitive. Ask a `Choice` over the available models, with the task text
and the state as the question's state. Ask any further judgments you find useful
(difficulty, whether it touches a build or install path, how much code it must
read) as separate questions in the same request, since independent questions run
in parallel. Use the returned probabilities: a low-confidence pick is worth
recording in the ledger, not worth blocking on.

**Four exclusions, decided by rule and never sent to Jev:**

1. **Web research is `agy`.** It replaces web search; when the work is research
   on the open web, that is the answer without asking.
2. **The claude binary** where the work must be Claude, including a coordinator.
3. **Writing a spec goes to Fable, or to Pro through the relay.** Not Jev's
   choice.
4. Anything Rolf pins by hand, if he ever does.

**Failure escalates itself.** A lane that fails asks again with the failure as
part of the state, and gets a stronger model. No settings edit, no permission
step, no `escalate` list a coordinator may not touch. Bound the escalation so it
cannot climb forever, and record each escalation in the ledger.

**Review keeps its place in the flow.** `round advance` still starts a review.
Its model comes from the same picker, reading what is actually being reviewed —
not from `[roles.reviewer]`.

**The roles table goes.** `[roles.*]` in `~/.config/herdr-ade/config.toml` is
deleted along with the code that reads it. `[recipes.*]` stays: it is the list of
models the picker chooses from, and each row needs whatever description Jev needs
to choose well. `doctor` refuses a config that still has `[roles.*]`, naming what
to remove. Update `skill/COORDINATOR.md`: the section on model choice becomes
"you do not choose; describe the work well, because that description is what
picks the model", and `docs/operations.md` to match.

Do not edit `~/.config/herdr-ade/config.toml` yourself. Say in your report
exactly what has to change there and the coordinator does it at install.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, the full test suite, clippy with warnings denied, all with
`PATH=/bin:$PATH DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`. Tests with a
faked Jev response for: a pick, each of the four exclusions, an escalation after
a failure, the escalation bound, a review getting its model from the picker, and
`doctor` refusing a leftover roles table. Do not make a live Jev call part of the
test suite.

# t-0077 report: U1 cost, U4 staleness and U5 task list on the screen

Branch `hp/adeherdr/t-0077-u1-u4-u5-cost-staleness-and-the-task-lis`.

## What landed

Three read-only additions to the talk overview (`src/talk/`). Every row is a
`Row`, so the compact view clips it to one line and the full overview (`F2`)
wraps it, exactly like the existing six sections. Opened in the order:

```
Stale (only when non-empty)
Goal
What you get at the end
How far along
Cost
Running now
Finished lately
Tasks
Needs you
```

### U5 — the task list

- New `src/talk/tasks.rs` parses the same file the digest reads,
  `<project>/TASKS.md` (`coordinator.rs` prints it verbatim; the screen reads
  the file directly, not a second copy).
- Format, from `skill/COORDINATOR.md` line 71: `##` headings are lists, each
  open task is `- [ ] <title> (<owner>)`, and a delegated task is
  `(agent → t-0007)`. `- [x]` and any other line are ignored.
- `Overview::load` builds one `Heading` row per non-empty list, then one row
  per task: the owner is the leading word, the title is the body, and a
  delegated task's thread state (`working` / `checking` / `needs you`, the
  same words `Running now` uses) is the right-hand marker. The thread state
  comes from the same single herdr poll already used for the lanes
  (`Live::group`), not a second poll.
- Empty list -> no heading; no tasks at all -> `No tasks are on the list.`;
  unreadable file -> `I could not read the task list.` Adding, finishing and
  cancelling stay Rolf's words in chat.

### U4 — staleness

- New `src/talk/stale.rs` returns `Stale { items }`; each item is `what` plus
  an exact `remedy`. `Overview` only renders the section when an item exists,
  so a clean run shows no `Stale` heading at all.
- The seven checks:
  1. **This talk shell** — the running build id (`crate::VERSION`) against the
     installed `~/.local/bin/herdr-ade --version`. Remedy: "Restart this
     screen: press Ctrl+C, then run `ha talk <slug>`."
  2. **The client window** — `herdr status client --json` version against
     `herdr --version`. Remedy: reopen the client window.
  3. **The local herdr server** — `herdr status server --json`; the fork
     already reports `server_binary_stale` / `restart_needed`. Remedy:
     `herdr server restart`.
  4. **The box's herdr server** — the same probe over
     `remote::ssh` to the SSH target of the project's remote machine. Remedy:
     `ssh <target> herdr server restart`.
  5. **The coordinator's skill** — the SHA-256 of `skill/COORDINATOR.md` on
     disk against the hash recorded when the coordinator was primed.
  6. **A running lane's skill** — the same per unresolved lane, using its
     recorded role skill (`skill/LANE.md` etc.). Remedy: restart that lane.
  7. **pi's provider port** — `providers.pro.baseUrl` in
     `<ADE root>/pi/agent/models.json` against `port` in
     `<ADE root>/pro-bridge/serve.json`. Remedy: `herdr-pi setup`.

  the existing three-second live poll; the screen never runs the SSH probe
  every frame. Every source is best effort: an unreadable file or failed
  command produces no row, never a guessed one.

**One record addition backs items 5 and 6.** Nothing recorded what an agent was
primed with, so `Launch` gained `#[serde(default)] skill_hash: String`; it is
set from `lane::skill_text(role)` at every start (`launch_from` for lanes,
`launch_recipe` now takes the role for the coordinator and adopt). Old records
deserialize with an empty hash and are never called stale. `lane::skill_text`
and `lane::skill_file` are now the single source for both what `ha skill`
prints and what staleness compares.

- New `src/talk/cost.rs`. pi writes one `message.usage` object per assistant
  message (`totalTokens`, `cost.total`); the lane's session directory is named
  after its worktree, so each thread is mapped by `thread.worktree_path` to
  `<ADE root>/pi/agent/sessions/--<path>--`. Tokens, money and the span of the
  day's messages (whole minutes) are summed per lane. `herdr-pro`
  `usage.jsonl` lines carry only a timestamp/lane/tag, so they count as sends
  with the cost marked unknown.
- The section shows `today` and `round <r>` (the newest round whose merge has
  not landed, summed over its manifest members). When only time is known the
  row reads `N min, cost unknown`; a remote lane with no local session is
  unknown, not zero. Empty -> `No cost has been recorded yet.`
- Per-lane totals are recorded in `Cost.lanes`; the section draws the day and
  round totals the brief names.
